body:
I feel like this should be at least somewhat integrated with the following paragraph?

> The [networking task source](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#networking-task-source) [tasks](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-task) to process the data as it is being fetched must each [immediately](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#immediately) queue a [media element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#media-element) task given the media element to run the first appropriate steps from the [media data processing steps list](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#media-data-processing-steps-list) below. (A new task is used for this so that the work described below occurs relative to the appropriate media element event task source rather than using the [networking task source](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#networking-task-source).)

similarly I wonder if

> When the [networking task source](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#networking-task-source) has [queued](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#queue-a-task) the last [task](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-task) as part of fetching the [media resource](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#media-resource) (i.e. once the download has completed), if the fetching process completes without errors, including decoding the media data, and if all of the data is available to the user agent without network access, then, the user agent must move on to the final step below. This might never happen, e.g. when streaming an infinite resource such as web radio, or if the resource is longer than the user agent's ability to cache data.

should be part of processResponseEndOfBody.

body:
The paragraph below this about

> The user agent may use whatever means necessary to fetch the resource (within the constraints put forward by this and other specifications); for example, reconnecting to the server in the face of network errors, using HTTP range retrieval requests, or switching to a streaming protocol. The user agent must consider a resource erroneous only if it has given up trying to fetch it.

seems a bit contradictory and redundant with the new rigorous specification. For example the rigorous specification seems to imply it should finalize and report timing on the first network error.

Probably the best we can do here is monkey-patch our own rigorous steps a bit. Maybe something like this?

> Although the above steps give an algorithm for issuing requests, the user agent may use other means besides those exact ones, especially in the face of error conditions. For example, the user agent may reconnect to the server or switch to a streaming protocol. The user agent must only consider the resource erroneous, and proceed into the error branches of the above steps, if the user agent has given up trying to fetch the resource.

body:
Is the requirement that `end` match `byteRange[1]` when not "until end" necessary?
It seems inconsistent with allowing a truncated response with "until end".

[The 206 (Partial Content) status code indicates that the server is successfully fulfilling a range request for the target resource by transferring one or more parts of the selected representation that correspond to the satisfiable ranges found in the request's Range header field (Section 3.1).](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc7233.html#status.206).  i.e. I'm not aware of any requirement that a response should include the entirety of a requested range.

There is [precendent](https://wicg.github.io/background-fetch/#validate-partial-response-algorithm) for expecting a response containing only a portion of the requested range to be aligned with the start of the requested range, so I guess that would be less problematic.

body:
Apparently implementations today don't verify that the request range matches the response range.
Added a [PR](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/7782) to remove that verification.

Also, Gecko & Chromium allow 200 responses for range requests. Added that to the PR. It's a known bug in Safari.
